```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)

t1 <- out("table_1_study1_conditions.csv")
t3 <- out("table_3_study1_gun_support.csv")
t4 <- out("table_4_study2_conditions.csv")
t5 <- out("table_5_study2_amount.csv")
t6 <- out("table_6_study2_favor.csv")
t7 <- out("table_7_study3_conditions.csv")
t8 <- out("table_8_study3_support.csv")

# Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed here, from the deposited
# archive, at the time this document is rendered. That includes the numbers that were
# not wrong: a token carried over from the published sentence is inherited on trust,
# and rendering the whole sentence from the pipeline is what verifies it.
cell <- function(d, grp, trm, column = "estimate") {
  hits <- d[[column]][d$group == grp & d$term == trm]
  stopifnot(length(hits) == 1)
  hits
}

group_n <- function(d, grp) {
  hits <- unique(d$N[str_detect(d$group, grp)])
  stopifnot(length(hits) == 1)
  hits
}

# The article states its Study 3 scale-point effects to three decimals and its
# p-values to two, so the corrected sentences keep that precision. Minus signs are
# set as the en dash the published page uses.
pt3 <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.3f", x), "^-", "–")
pt2 <- function(x) str_replace(sprintf("%.2f", x), "^-", "–")
comma <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

# The published sentence does its arithmetic on its own printed inputs, three decimals
# each, and so does the corrected one: 2·0.074 + 2·0.040 is 0.228, where the unrounded
# inputs give 0.227. maintained/in_text_claims.R computes the claim the same way.
swing <- function(d, grp) {
  2 * (round(cell(d, grp, "positive_information"), 3) -
         round(cell(d, grp, "negative_information"), 3))
}

# The opening paragraph counts the entries in words, as prose does, so the count is
# spelled from the spine rather than typed beside it.
spell <- function(n) {
  c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
    "eleven", "twelve")[n]
}

# Entry 1's correction is the float below rather than a sentence, so its corrected values
# are the cells that table prints and not tokens inside a [[...]] span. The twelve claim ids
# and the twelve values are generated from one map here, in one order, because a hand-typed
# pair of parallel lists is the thing that goes wrong: the ids and the values would still
# have the right lengths after a transposition and nothing would read as broken.
favor_cells <- tribble(
  ~claim_id,                     ~group,                       ~term,
  "study2_favor_opp_pos_unadj",  "Opponents (No Covariates)",  "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_opp_neg_unadj",  "Opponents (No Covariates)",  "negative_information",
  "study2_favor_opp_pos_adj",    "Opponents (Covariates)",     "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_opp_neg_adj",    "Opponents (Covariates)",     "negative_information",
  "study2_favor_mod_pos_unadj",  "Moderates (No Covariates)",  "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_mod_neg_unadj",  "Moderates (No Covariates)",  "negative_information",
  "study2_favor_mod_pos_adj",    "Moderates (Covariates)",     "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_mod_neg_adj",    "Moderates (Covariates)",     "negative_information",
  "study2_favor_pro_pos_unadj",  "Proponents (No Covariates)", "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_pro_neg_unadj",  "Proponents (No Covariates)", "negative_information",
  "study2_favor_pro_pos_adj",    "Proponents (Covariates)",    "positive_information",
  "study2_favor_pro_neg_adj",    "Proponents (Covariates)",    "negative_information"
) |>
  mutate(value = map2_chr(group, term, \(g, t) sprintf("%.2f", cell(t6, g, t))))

# The minus sign here is the hyphen the extraction writes, not the en dash the page sets:
# this column is compared as a number by maintained/in_text_claims.R, where the note's
# typography is the wrong convention. The float above keeps the page's en dash.

# Entry 1's note answers what the corrected table was holding up: p. 1506 says of it that
# "with the exception of negative information among opponents, all these coefficients are
# statistically significant." Read against the table the page printed (Table 5's contents)
# and against the corrected one, cell by cell, at the page's own 0.1 threshold.
info_cells <- function(d) {
  d |>
    filter(term %in% c("positive_information", "negative_information")) |>
    mutate(opponents_negative = str_detect(group, "^Opponents") &
             term == "negative_information",
           signed = if_else(term == "positive_information", estimate > 0, estimate < 0))
}
fav <- info_cells(t6)
stopifnot(nrow(fav) == 12, all(fav$signed),
          all(fav$p.value[fav$opponents_negative] >= 0.1),
          all(fav$p.value[!fav$opponents_negative] < 0.1))
amt <- info_cells(t5)
amt_opp_pos <- amt |> filter(group == "Opponents (No Covariates)", term == "positive_information")
amt_opp_neg <- amt |> filter(group == "Opponents (Covariates)", term == "negative_information")
fav_opp_neg <- fav |> filter(opponents_negative) |> arrange(desc(str_detect(group, "No Covariates")))
stopifnot(amt_opp_pos$p.value >= 0.1, amt_opp_neg$p.value < 0.05)
est_p <- function(e, p) str_glue("{pt2(e)} (p = {sprintf('%.2f', p)})")

# Entry 9 is the corrigendum's Table 1. Its note says what the corrected standard
# deviations do to the sentence on p. 1502 that they "do not appear to vary by treatment
# condition and are very precisely estimated." T2 Belief is binary, so its standard
# deviation follows its mean.
t1_row <- function(cond, column) {
  hits <- t1[[column]][t1$condition == cond]
  stopifnot(length(hits) == 1)
  hits
}
belief_gap <- t1_row("Negative Information", "W2_Q1_sd") - t1_row("Positive Information", "W2_Q1_sd")
belief_gap_se <- sqrt(t1_row("Negative Information", "W2_Q1_sd_bse")^2 +
                        t1_row("Positive Information", "W2_Q1_sd_bse")^2)
attitude_sd <- range(t1$W2_scale_sd)

opp_pos <- cell(t8, "Opponents (Covariates)", "positive_information")
opp_neg <- cell(t8, "Opponents (Covariates)", "negative_information")
opp_p <- cell(t8, "Opponents (Covariates)", "negative_information", "p.value")
pro_pos <- cell(t8, "Proponents (Covariates)", "positive_information")
pro_neg <- cell(t8, "Proponents (Covariates)", "negative_information")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every correction is defined once, here, and rendered from this
# tibble: into this note, and into errata_entries.csv at the bottom of the file, which
# is what the README's count and any later remastered edition read. Before the spine
# existed the same corrections were written out in prose in more than one place, which
# is how two copies of one list drift apart without either looking wrong.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, and is the only markup a field carries. Each
# renderer resolves it its own way: bold here, \was{} in an edition. Everything else in
# a field (escaped asterisks, en dashes, middots) is literal text, so the same string
# can be set by either renderer.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY. An entry number can already have been cited by a reader, so
# a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved, merged or renumbered.
#
# `form` is an editorial judgment about the entry rather than a fact about this page's
# typesetting: "full" where the published and corrected fields are whole sentences that
# need setting as blocks, "brief" where the entry is a token replacement.
#
# `location` is where the defect sits in the published article, quoted from the section or
# float heading that ground_truth/published_claims.csv gives for the claim the entry
# corrects, prefixed with "published". This document never prints it: it is carried for the
# CSV, which a remastered edition reads. Left empty the column arrives there as a logical
# NA rather than a string, which is why every row carries one.
#
# `claim_ids` names the ground truth rows the entry corrects, semicolon separated, and it is
# what makes "has this finding been published?" a query over the corpus rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where the entry has no ground truth row: a reference list is not
# an extraction claim. Every id listed here is checked against the ground truth by
# ground_truth/claims_gate.R, which refuses to finish on a dangling one.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "float", "pipeline", "full",
  "Table 6 reprints Table 5",
  "published Table 6, p. 1506",
  "Table 6, \"Effects of information on favoring minimum wage raise,\" prints [[the contents of Table 5]], every cell identical, under a column header reading [[\"Dependent variable: T2 Amount\"]].",
  "[[This edition prints the Table 6 models the deposited GC_Study_2_analysis.R fits]], on favor_T2_recode, which are the estimates Figure 1's \"Study 2: T2 Favor\" panel plots.",
  paste(
    "Table 6, \"Effects of information on favoring minimum wage raise,\" prints the",
    "contents of Table 5 rather than its own. Every cell is identical to Table 5's, and",
    "the column header inside Table 6 reads \"Dependent variable: T2 Amount\" where the",
    "table is captioned for the Favor outcome. The text is correct and the table is not:",
    "the deposited `GC_Study_2_analysis.R` fits its Table 6 models on `favor_T2_recode`,",
    "and Figure 1's \"Study 2: T2 Favor\" panel plots the estimates below rather than the",
    "ones Table 6 prints.") |>
  str_c(str_glue(
    " The sentence after the table on p. 1506, \"With the exception of negative ",
    "information among opponents, all these coefficients are statistically ",
    "significant,\" is false twice of the table the page prints: among opponents ",
    "positive information without covariates is {est_p(amt_opp_pos$estimate, amt_opp_pos$p.value)}, ",
    "and negative information with covariates is {est_p(amt_opp_neg$estimate, amt_opp_neg$p.value)}. ",
    "Of the corrected table it holds cell for cell. All twelve information ",
    "coefficients are correctly signed, and the only two not significant at the 0.1 ",
    "level are opponents' negative information, ",
    "{est_p(fav_opp_neg$estimate[1], fav_opp_neg$p.value[1])} without covariates and ",
    "{est_p(fav_opp_neg$estimate[2], fav_opp_neg$p.value[2])} with them. The correction ",
    "makes the text true. The corrected table follows.")),
  str_c(favor_cells$claim_id, collapse = ";"),
  str_c(favor_cells$value, collapse = ";"),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The Study 3 participant counts",
  "published Study 3, p. 1506",
  "A total of [[683]] subjects participated in the main survey (287 proponents and [[396]] opponents).",
  str_glue("A total of [[{sum(t7$n)}]] subjects participated in the main survey (287 proponents and [[{group_n(t8, 'Opponents')}]] opponents)."),
  str_glue(
    "The article's own Table 7 gives the six condition sizes as 117, 116, 112, 118, 121 ",
    "and 102, which sum to {sum(t7$n)}, and Tables 8 and 9 report ",
    "{group_n(t8, 'Opponents')} opponents. The deposited Study 3 data hold {sum(t7$n)} ",
    "rows, of which {group_n(t8, 'Proponents')} are proponents, ",
    "{group_n(t8, 'Opponents')} are opponents, and four carry no pre-treatment ",
    "classification and so appear in Table 7 but in neither regression table."),
  "study3_N_main;study3_N_opponents_text",
  str_c(sum(t7$n), ";", group_n(t8, "Opponents")),

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The Study 2 participant count",
  "published Study 2: Procedure, p. 1504",
  "Of the 1,500 recruited to the main survey, [[1,170]] participated.",
  str_glue("Of the 1,500 recruited to the main survey, [[{comma(sum(t4$n))}]] participated."),
  str_glue(
    "The article's own Table 4 gives the seven condition sizes as 93, 162, 165, 195, 169, ",
    "192 and 193, which sum to {comma(sum(t4$n))}, and the deposited Study 2 data hold ",
    "{comma(sum(t4$n))} rows."),
  "study2_N_participated",
  as.character(sum(t4$n)),

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The Study 3 positive information estimate among opponents",
  "published Study 3: Results, p. 1509",
  "Focusing on the covariate-adjusted models, we estimate that a one-unit increase in positive information causes an average increase in support for capital punishment of 0.015 scale points among proponents and [[0.068]] scale points among opponents, neither of which is statistically significant.",
  str_glue(
    "Focusing on the covariate-adjusted models, we estimate that a one-unit increase in ",
    "positive information causes an average increase in support for capital punishment of ",
    "{pt3(pro_pos)} scale points among proponents and [[{pt3(opp_pos)}]] scale points ",
    "among opponents, neither of which is statistically significant."),
  str_glue(
    "The published sentence gives 0.068 for opponents. The specification the deposit fits, ",
    "and which Table 8's fourth column reports, gives {pt3(opp_pos)}. Both round to the ",
    "0.07 that Table 8 prints, so the disagreement is visible only at the precision the ",
    "text itself uses. Dropping race from the covariate set gives 0.086, so the published ",
    "figure comes from neither specification."),
  "study3_text_opp_pos_adj",
  sprintf("%.3f", opp_pos),

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The Study 3 negative information estimate among opponents",
  "published Study 3: Results, p. 1509",
  "Negative information has a strong negative effect among proponents (–0.326, p < 0.01), and a weakly negative effect among opponents ([[–0.042]], p = [[0.43]]).",
  str_glue(
    "Negative information has a strong negative effect among proponents ({pt3(pro_neg)}, ",
    "p < 0.01), and a weakly negative effect among opponents ([[{pt3(opp_neg)}]], ",
    "p = [[{pt2(opp_p)}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "The published sentence gives –0.042 and p = 0.43. Table 8's own fourth column, and ",
    "the deposited specification behind it, give {pt3(opp_neg)} with p = {pt2(opp_p)}. ",
    "The estimate is not significant at any conventional level on either figure."),
  "study3_text_opp_neg_adj;study3_text_opp_neg_pvalue",
  str_c(sprintf("%.3f", opp_neg), ";", sprintf("%.2f", opp_p)),

  6, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The Study 3 movement from Con Con to Pro Pro among opponents",
  "published Study 3: Results, p. 1509",
  "These estimates imply that moving from the Con Con condition to the Pro Pro condition would cause proponents to move 2·0.015 + 2·0.326 = 0.682 scale points and opponents to move 2·[[0.068]] + 2·[[0.042]] = [[0.220]] scale points.",
  str_glue(
    "These estimates imply that moving from the Con Con condition to the Pro Pro condition ",
    "would cause proponents to move 2·{pt3(pro_pos)} + 2·{pt3(abs(pro_neg))} = ",
    "{pt3(swing(t8, 'Proponents (Covariates)'))} scale points and opponents to move ",
    "2·[[{pt3(opp_pos)}]] + 2·[[{pt3(abs(opp_neg))}]] = ",
    "[[{pt3(swing(t8, 'Opponents (Covariates)'))}]] scale points."),
  str_glue(
    "The published sentence gives 2·0.068 + 2·0.042 = 0.220. The arithmetic is right and ",
    "the two inputs are the ones corrected in entries 4 and 5, so the total moves with ",
    "them. It is computed from the inputs as printed, as the published total was; from ",
    "their unrounded values it is {pt3(2 * (opp_pos - opp_neg))}."),
  "study3_text_opp_swing",
  sprintf("%.3f", swing(t8, "Opponents (Covariates)")),

  7, "cross_reference", "pipeline", "full",
  "The cross-reference to the binary support results",
  "published Study 1: Results, p. 1503",
  "In [[Table 2]], we turn to the binary gun control support dependent variable, which asks whether respondents support 'stricter gun control laws in the United States.'",
  "In [[Table 3]], we turn to the binary gun control support dependent variable, which asks whether respondents support 'stricter gun control laws in the United States.'",
  paste(
    "Table 2 is the composite scale table, discussed in the preceding paragraph, which",
    "opens with the same words. The binary support models are Table 3."),
  "study1_table_3_reference",
  "3",

  8, "typography", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The significance threshold in the Table 2 note",
  "published Table 2 note, p. 1502",
  "\\*p < 0.1; \\*\\*p < 0.05; \\*\\*\\*p [[>]] 0.01",
  "\\*p < 0.1; \\*\\*p < 0.05; \\*\\*\\*p [[<]] 0.01",
  str_glue(
    "Three stars mark the most significant cells, not the least. Table 3's note, on the ",
    "facing page, states the same threshold correctly. The starred cells are unaffected: ",
    "the three-star coefficients in these tables have p-values of ",
    "{sprintf('%.4f', cell(t3, 'Among Proponents (No Covariates)', 'Z_informationcon_information', 'p.value'))} ",
    "and below."),
  "study1_table_2_note_threshold",
  NA_character_,

  # The corrigendum's correction, carried so this note is a complete account of what the
  # published article gets wrong (as peyton_huber_coppock_2022 carries its corrigendum's).
  # Its corrected side is the authors' own table, so no claim's value moves: the two claims
  # it names count how many of the corrigendum's cells the deposit reproduces.
  9, "corrigendum", "publisher record", "full",
  "Table 1's standard deviations",
  "published Table 1, p. 1502",
  "Table 1 prints [[the standard errors of the means]] in its two SD columns, [[(0.00)]] as their standard errors, and [[no condition label]] on its first row.",
  "[[Table 1 as the corrigendum corrects it]]: the standard deviation of each outcome in each condition, with its bootstrapped standard error, and the first row labelled Control.",
  str_glue(
    "A corrigendum the authors published at *British Journal of Political Science* 50(4), ",
    "1517, doi 10.1017/S0007123419000024, ",
    "corrects Table 1 for a coding error that made the standard deviations and their ",
    "standard errors inaccurate, and this edition sets its table. The SD columns the ",
    "page prints repeat the standard errors of the means beside them. The corrected T2 ",
    "Attitude standard deviations run from {sprintf('%.2f', attitude_sd[1])} to ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', attitude_sd[2])}, which bears out the text's \"the standard ",
    "deviations of the outcomes do not appear to vary by treatment condition and are very ",
    "precisely estimated.\" The T2 Belief standard deviations do vary, and could not fail ",
    "to: the outcome is binary, so its standard deviation follows its mean, and means of ",
    "{sprintf('%.2f', t1_row('Negative Information', 'W2_Q1_mean'))} under negative ",
    "information and {sprintf('%.2f', t1_row('Positive Information', 'W2_Q1_mean'))} under ",
    "positive give ",
    "standard deviations of {sprintf('%.2f', t1_row('Negative Information', 'W2_Q1_sd'))} ",
    "and {sprintf('%.2f', t1_row('Positive Information', 'W2_Q1_sd'))}, a difference ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', belief_gap / belief_gap_se)} times its bootstrapped standard error. ",
    "No estimate in the article uses these standard deviations."),
  "study1_table_1_cells;study1_table_1_boot_cells",
  NA_character_,

  # Entries 10 and 11 come from the reference audit's re-run of 2026-10-29, which learned to
  # read a page range printed as its first page alone. Each corrected range is given in full,
  # as the list gives nearly all of its others. A reference list is not an extraction claim,
  # so neither has a claim_id or moves a value.
  10, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Chipman, George and McCulloch (2007) reference prints a first page in place of a page range",
  "published references, p. 1513",
  "Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 19, [[265]].",
  "Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 19, [[265–272]].",
  paste("Crossref, doi 10.7551/mitpress/7503.003.0038, gives the chapter's pages in",
        "Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 19 as 265 to 272."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  11, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Gelman and Loken (2016) reference prints a first page in place of a page range",
  "published references, p. 1514",
  "The Best Writing on Mathematics 2015, [[305]].",
  "The Best Writing on Mathematics 2015, [[305–318]].",
  paste("Crossref, doi 10.1515/9781400873371-028, gives the chapter's pages in The Best",
        "Writing on Mathematics 2015 as 305 to 318."),
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with what the entry actually publishes ----
# The column and the correction are built from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value.
#
# A sentence entry is checked against its own [[...]] spans, by position where the counts
# line up and against SOME span where they do not, since an entry may mark a label as well
# as a number. Entry 1 is exempt because its correction is the float below rather than a
# sentence: its spans are prose naming the defect and carry no numbers at all. What stands
# in for the check there is that its ids and its values are generated from one map, in one
# order, a few chunks above.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

# A sentence sets a number the way the page sets it, with an en dash for the minus sign and
# a comma between the thousands. The column sets it the way the extraction writes it, since
# maintained/in_text_claims.R compares that column as a number and parses neither. Both are
# typography rather than part of the value, so they are normalised away before the
# containment test instead of being allowed to decide it. Everything else about the value,
# its precision above all, still has to match.
as_compared <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("\u2013", "-") |>
    str_replace_all("(?<=\\d),(?=\\d{3})", "")
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

sentences <- quantified |> filter(class != "float")

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(sentences, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(as_compared(s), fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(as_compared(s), fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(sentences |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# Entry 1's values are the cells the corrected float prints, so they are checked against the
# table's own source rather than against prose.
stopifnot(identical(
  str_split(entries$corrected_values[entries$entry == 1], ";")[[1]],
  favor_cells$value
))

# An entry that moves a claim's value has to say what the value becomes, and an entry that
# moves none may not carry one. Three classes move a value here: a quantity in a sentence,
# the float that reprints the wrong table, and the cross-reference whose claim is the table
# number itself. A typography entry changes a comparison operator and no claim's value, so
# it carries NA. maintained/in_text_claims.R is passed this same list as quantity_classes.
moves_value <- c("quantity", "float", "cross_reference")
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class %in% moves_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[!entries$class %in% moves_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | !is.na(entries$claim_ids))
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it its own way.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` corrections to "Does Counter-Attitudinal Information Cause Backlash? Results from Three Large Survey Experiments," published in the *British Journal of Political Science* 50(4), doi [10.1017/S0007123418000327](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007123418000327). **None of them changes a conclusion of the paper.** The first is a table printed in place of another; three are participant counts that disagree with the article's own tables; three are Study 3 estimates restated in the text at a precision the tables do not show; one is a cross-reference; one is a significance threshold; one is the authors' own corrigendum to Table 1; and the last two are reference-list entries that print a first page in place of a page range. The article's finding, that treatment effects across all three experiments run in the direction of the information rather than against it, is unaffected, and Figure 1 already plots the corrected Table 6 estimates rather than the ones that table prints.

Entry 9 is the correction a separate corrigendum made, at *British Journal of Political Science* 50(4), 1517, doi [10.1017/S0007123419000024](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0007123419000024), to the standard deviations of Table 1. It is carried here so this note is a complete account of what the published article gets wrong.

Every number in a corrected sentence below is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/J7WNTM](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/J7WNTM)) at the time this document is rendered, including the numbers that were not wrong. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/guess_coppock_2020](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/guess_coppock_2020). Bold marks what has changed.

One published figure is deliberately absent from this list. The article reports that "93 per cent of subjects have a positive treatment effect estimate when exposed to positive information." The deposited BART script sets no seed, so that figure is a single unseeded draw and the right comparison is against the spread of draws rather than against a point. Refitting at ten seeds under a current sampler puts the proportion between 97.7 and 99.6 per cent, above the published figure in every run, which is a discrepancy worth recording but not a number that can be corrected to a value the analysis would reproduce. It is documented in the repository's report instead.

```{r entry-1, results="asis"}
# The correction here is the float below, not a sentence, so the row's prose is its
# note; the published and corrected fields name the defect for other renderers.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 1)
cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r table6}
star <- function(p) {
  case_when(p < 0.01 ~ "***", p < 0.05 ~ "**", p < 0.1 ~ "*", .default = "")
}

fmt <- function(est, p) paste0(str_replace(sprintf("%.2f", est), "^-", "–"), star(p))
fmt_se <- function(se) paste0("(", sprintf("%.2f", se), ")")

label_of <- c("positive_information" = "Pos. Info (0 to 1)",
              "negative_information" = "Neg. Info (0 to 1)",
              `I(condition_type == "Placebo")TRUE` = "Condition: Placebo",
              "(Intercept)" = "Constant")

groups <- c("Opponents (No Covariates)", "Opponents (Covariates)",
            "Moderates (No Covariates)", "Moderates (Covariates)",
            "Proponents (No Covariates)", "Proponents (Covariates)")

body <- map(names(label_of), function(trm) {
  est <- map_chr(groups, ~ fmt(cell(t6, .x, trm), cell(t6, .x, trm, "p.value")))
  se <- map_chr(groups, ~ fmt_se(cell(t6, .x, trm, "std.error")))
  bind_rows(
    tibble(term = label_of[[trm]], value = est, group = groups),
    tibble(term = "", value = se, group = groups)
  ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = value)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

covar <- tibble(term = "Covariates") |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.list(rep(c("No", "Yes"), 3)), groups)))
ns <- tibble(term = "N") |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.list(map_chr(groups, ~ as.character(unique(t6$N[t6$group == .x])))), groups)))
r2 <- tibble(term = "$R^2$") |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(setNames(as.list(map_chr(groups, function(g) {
    sprintf("%.2f", unique(t6$r2[t6$group == g]))
  })), groups)))

tab <- bind_rows(body, covar, ns, r2)

kable(tab, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", escape = FALSE,
      align = c("l", rep("r", 6)), col.names = c(" ", rep(c("", ""), 3)),
      caption = "Table 6, corrected. Effects of information on favoring minimum wage raise. Dependent variable: T2 Favor. Robust standard errors are in parentheses. The information content of the Placebo condition is coded 0. Covariates include T1 Amount, T1 Favor, age, gender, ideology, party ID, and education. *p < 0.1; **p < 0.05; ***p < 0.01") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Among opponents" = 2, "Among moderates" = 2,
                                 "Among proponents" = 2), escape = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r quoted-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every entry opens with
# one; without it the "## 2." lands in the page as literal text.
walk(2:max(entries$entry), function(i) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == i)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. The README's
# count reads it rather than keeping its own, so the two cannot drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
